title: A Compass for the Monsoon
premise: Edmund Villalobos, a bush pilot grounded by a broken plane and a debt to the wrong people, ferries medicine upriver by boat just as the monsoon season turns violent. When a low tide exposes a sea cave said to hold the wreck of a smuggler's fleet, Edmund discovers her late father's compass points not north but toward it — and that the man helping her navigate, a quiet salvager named Ilya, has been paid by her creditors to find the cave first. As storms trap them together and the truth of their competing loyalties surfaces, Edmund must choose between paying her debt with the cave's treasure or burning her ledger and claiming an uncharted life. In the end she scuttles the treasure's location beneath rising water, settles her debt with honesty instead of gold, and flies out on a repaired plane with Ilya beside her — belonging, at last, chosen rather than owed.
about_author: Felix Nakamura is the pen name of a former cargo pilot turned novelist who spent six years flying supply runs across Southeast Asian river deltas. Their fiction blends cockpit-precise adventure with meditations on drift, debt, and the maps we inherit from family.

chapters.title: The Weight of North
chapters.summary: POV: Edmund. Grounded with a busted engine and a creditor's deadline, Edmund loads medicine into a borrowed boat and inherits her father's brass compass from a lawyer who warns her it 'doesn't point where you'd want.' At low tide she glimpses a cave mouth on a chartless island. Emotional beat: restless obligation — a woman held in place by debts she never chose.

chapters.title: Salt and Silence
chapters.summary: POV: Edmund. A leaking hull forces Edmund to accept help from Ilya, a salvager who knows the waters too well. They shelter from the first squall; he deflects every question about why he's heading the same direction. The compass needle trembles toward the cave. Emotional beat: wary intimacy — trust forming inside a lie neither can name yet.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Edmund/Ilya. Inside the cave they find the smuggler wreck — and Ilya's contract papers naming Edmund's creditors. Betrayal detonates mid-storm; the monsoon makes landfall, sealing them in as the cave floods. Edmund nearly drowns retrieving the one thing that matters: her father's logbook proving the debt was forged. Emotional beat: climax — loyalty shattered, truth surfaced like a hull.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: POV: Edmund. Storm-bound together, Edmund and Ilya strike a bargain: expose the forged debt, sink the treasure's location under silt and secrecy. When skies clear, creditors arrive to nothing but rising water. Her plane is repaired; she offers Ilya the spare seat. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging chosen freely, a compass finally pointing somewhere worth going.
